**The meaning of the verse**
﴿وَلَا تَتَمَنَّوْا مَا فَضَّلَ اللَّهُ بِهِ بَعْضَكُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ ۚ لِّلرِّجَالِ نَصِيبٌ مِّمَّا اكْتَسَبُوا ۖ وَلِلنِّسَاءِ نَصِيبٌ مِّمَّا اكْتَسَبْنَ ۚ وَاسْأَلُوا اللَّهَ مِن فَضْلِهِ ۗ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمًا﴾
And do not wish for that by which Allah has favoured some of you over others, in talents, provision and other things. Allah has made for men a set share of reward according to their deeds, and for women a share of what they have done. And ask Allah, the Generous, the Bestower, to give you of His bounty, instead of wishing. Allah knows all things, and He knows best what is good for His servants in the good He has shared out among them.

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. Why did Nizar stand far away from the kite and wish it would tear? And was he happy when it tore?
2. Grandma Umm Fawzi said, "You wished for it to be taken away from him; you didn't wish to have one like it." What is the difference between the two? (Wishing for a blessing to be taken away from its owner is blameworthy envy. Better is what the verse says: ask Allah of His bounty, and He gives to you without taking anything from your brother.)
3. What blessing had Allah given Nizar that he did not see? And how did it become a cause of joy for Fadi and the children of the village?

**This week's exercise**
Every evening this week your child mentions a blessing or a skill Allah has given them, and once uses one of them to make someone else happy, such as teaching a brother or sister or fixing a friend's toy. And if they admire something someone else has, they say, "O Allah, bless it for him, and give me of Your bounty."
